text.p: Renaissance Energy Ltd, on the heels of sharply higher year-to-date financial results, said it would increase its 1996 capital spending to C$875 million from C$825 million.

Renaissance, which reported nine-month earnings of C$127 million or C$1.16 per share, up from C$51 million or C$0.54 per share last year, said most of the spending increase came from two recent oil property purchases for a total of C$40 million.
The expenditure boost comes after an earlier upward revision in September.
Renaissance has said it planned to spend C$800 million in 1997 and drill 1,850 wells in western Canada.
However, a high proportion of spending on undeveloped land and property acquisitions, as in the last three years, was expected to tail off, it said.
"Our undeveloped land has quadrupled over this period and will enable us to maintain an aggressive drilling program for many years without significantly expanding the base," the company said.
Also, the large amount of capital raised by Canada's oil and gas sector this year is expected to make property purchases too expensice, Renaissance said.

Renaissance said it would focus its drilling on light oil opportunities because many of its competitors were directing their investment to heavy oil projects, which could cause oversupply. It also said it had a positive view of natural gas prices.

The company said it produced an average of 68,054 barrels per day oil oil in the first nine months, up from55,619 last year. Gas production averaged 388 million cubic feet per day, up from 355 million. -- Reuters Calgary Bureau 403 531-1624
